Re: Appeal of denial of total shoulder replacement  
CPT 23472  
Reference number: POC-3B4A598A17-15463  
Date of adverse benefit determination: 2026-08-11  

Dear Humana Appeals Reviewer:

I am appealing the denial of prior authorization for a total shoulder replacement, CPT 23472. The appeal deadline stated in the determination is February 7, 2027. Please treat this letter and the enclosed clinical records as my request for reconsideration.

The requested procedure is medically necessary because I have 14 months of progressive shoulder pain that has not improved with appropriate nonoperative treatment. I completed 12 weeks of supervised physical therapy, consisting of 24 visits from March 28, 2026, through June 20, 2026. The therapy focused on range of motion and periscapular strengthening, and the physical therapy discharge note documents completion of this treatment without adequate relief.

I also used NSAIDs for six months with inadequate improvement. A corticosteroid injection on April 6, 2026, provided only four weeks of partial relief. These measures have failed to provide durable symptom control.

The imaging demonstrates advanced structural joint disease. Shoulder radiographs obtained on June 12, 2026, using true AP and axillary views, show complete loss of the glenohumeral joint space, osteophytes, subchondral sclerosis, and a flattened glenoid. CT imaging confirms that the rotator cuff is intact. These findings support a severe glenohumeral arthritic process appropriate for consideration of total shoulder arthroplasty.

The condition substantially limits daily functioning. I cannot reach overhead, dress without help, or sleep on the affected side. Examination shows glenohumeral crepitus, active forward elevation limited to 90 degrees, and external rotation limited to 10 degrees. Cuff strength remains intact. The combination of severe imaging abnormalities, persistent pain, failed conservative treatment, and major functional impairment supports the requested operation.

There are no documented clinical factors that would make the procedure unsafe or medically inappropriate. I have no active infection or untreated substance use disorder. My BMI is 29, and I am a nonsmoker.

The treating orthopedic surgeon, Lindqvist, MD, has evaluated this condition and requested the procedure. I ask Humana to reverse the denial and authorize CPT 23472.

I was unable to identify a publicly available Humana Commercial/ACA medical policy containing the medical-necessity criteria applied to this request. Accordingly, this letter does not quote or interpret a Humana policy. If Humana maintains the denial, please provide the exact medical policy or clinical-review criteria used, the specific criteria that were considered unmet, the clinical rationale for the determination, and the medical records or information relied upon by the reviewer.

Please also arrange a peer-to-peer discussion with Lindqvist, MD, if requested by the reviewing physician. Please send the appeal determination and the criteria applied to the address listed above and to my provider.

Enclosures:

- Prior authorization denial notice
- Orthopedic evaluation by Lindqvist, MD
- Physical therapy discharge note documenting 24 visits from March 28, 2026, through June 20, 2026
- Medication and injection treatment history
- June 12, 2026, shoulder radiographs
- CT report confirming an intact rotator cuff
- Relevant examination and functional-limitation documentation

Sincerely,

Quinn Carter
